title: WINGS ICT Solutions says its wi.breathe AI camera system, during trial operation, detected the start of a fire in the Troizina area and alerted authorities; an undated, vendor-only claim
summary: Identical press-release text ran on 12 May 2026 (GOVNews, Newsbeast, Reporter.gr); WINGS's English post omits the detection; the municipality's site has no post on it. No date, place or responder.
account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor record 2026-05-12-c1ff says that WINGS ICT Solutions deployed its wi.breathe platform in Troizinia-Methana, Greece, and that 'the system enabled authorities to detect and prevent a fire within one minute'. The Monitor's eight listed Greek pages carry one text of 12 May 2026 announcing completion of the project: hybrid optical-thermal cameras at Vigla (Poros), Tsepeleni Aderon and Agios Georgios Methanon, a 'specially trained WINGS artificial-intelligence model', cloud infrastructure and 5G/4G networks, 24/7 surveillance, smoke and fire detection 'even within 1 minute', alerts in real time, and a quote from Mayor Anastasios Mougios thanking the company. Its only event claim is one sentence: that wi.breathe, 'already from its trial operation in the area, detected in real time the start of a fire in the Troizina area and immediately notified the competent authorities, preventing its spread'. The sentence gives no date, time, place, responder, Fire Service or Civil Protection statement, or size or damage figure; the 'within one minute' in the Monitor's summary is the release's capability claim. GOVNews bylines the text 'newsroom', Reporter.gr headlines it 'Wings:', and the earlier verifier found capital.gr labeling it a press release and Eleftheros Typos filing it under press releases (that page returned 403 here). WINGS's own English post of the same day (wings-ict-solutions.eu) announces 'the successful completion of the wi.breathe project' with the same sites and mayor's quote and omits the detection entirely; its product page says that 'wi.breathe.fire autonomous fire detection through AI and video analytics is deployed in Central Greece'. The municipality's website search for 'wi.breathe' returns only a 3 February 2025 post on a Best City Awards prize for the wi.BREATHE early fire-detection system, which names no detected fire; a search for 'fire Methana' returns a 13 June 2026 post on the mobilization and immediate extinguishing of a fire in a rough area of Methana, whose listing does not mention the cameras, and the earlier verifier found that the municipality's 2 July 2026 statement on a large fire between Agios Georgios and Agios Nikolaos on the Methana peninsula does not mention them either. No independent, dated account of the trial detection was found.
purpose: wi.breathe is sold for early wildfire detection and air-quality monitoring; the Troizinia-Methana installation was built to detect smoke and fire from hilltop cameras and alert civil-protection authorities, which is exactly the benefit claimed.
system: wi.breathe Operational Intelligence Platform (WINGS ICT Solutions): hybrid optical-thermal cameras, a WINGS-trained AI smoke and fire detection model, cloud infrastructure and 5G/4G links with dashboard, email and SMS alerts
deployer: Municipality of Troizinia-Methana (cameras at Vigla on Poros, Tsepeleni Aderon and Agios Georgios Methanon)
segment: Camera-based AI smoke and fire detection
taxonomy_note: No attributable event: the detection is one undated, unlocated sentence in a vendor press release, absent from the vendor's own English announcement and from the municipality's website, with no responder or official statement; the category is therefore general benefit and depths are null. The deployment itself (three camera sites, AI model, 5G/4G, completed May 2026) is documented by the release, the vendor's post and the municipality's 2025 award post. Unsupported: the fire's date, place, size, who responded and what 'preventing its spread' amounted to; the Monitor's 'within one minute' is a capability claim. Nothing is contradicted, because no checkable fact is asserted; later municipal fire statements (13 June and 2 July 2026) do not mention the cameras.

ratings.reason: No fire, response or avoided damage is documented outside the vendor's single undated sentence.
The municipality's own posts record the award (February 2025) and later fires (June and July 2026) without crediting the system; no response-time or cost figure is given.

ai_role.statement: The release describes a WINGS-trained AI model on optical-thermal camera feeds, and the product page describes autonomous detection through AI and video analytics, so the system is AI by the vendor's description. No source outside the vendor's text documents a detection, an alert or a response, so no contribution to any event can be assessed; the only sentence claiming one gives no date, place, responder or outcome.
